paper_title: Tying Word Vectors and Word Classifiers: A Loss Framework for Language Modeling

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for the paper's own proposed model?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports a word-level test perplexity of 68.5 on Penn Treebank for VD-LSTM+REAL (large), the paper's best LSTM model using both reused embeddings and augmented loss.

sub_questions.q: In what setting is that Penn Treebank test perplexity reported (single model, dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning)?
sub_questions.answer: The 68.5 test perplexity is for a single large 2-layer LSTM with 1500 units using variational dropout, reused embeddings, and augmented loss (VD-LSTM+REAL), with 51M parameters. The paper does not report dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning for this model.
sub_questions.quote: The best LSTM model (VD-LSTM+REAL) outperforms all previous work which uses conventional framework, including large ensembles.

sub_questions.q: How does the paper's own proposed model compare with the baselines listed in the paper on Penn Treebank word-level test perplexity?
sub_questions.answer: The paper states VD-LSTM+REAL (large) outperforms all previous work using the conventional framework, including large ensembles; Table 3 shows it ties VD-RHN at 68.5 test but is worse than VD-RHN+RE at 66.0. It is better than the listed cache baseline (92.0), pointer baseline (70.9), and ensemble baselines (68.7).
sub_questions.quote: The best LSTM model (VD-LSTM+REAL) outperforms all previous work which uses conventional framework, including large ensembles.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper report any model trained with the paper's reused-embedding framework that achieves a different Penn Treebank word-level test perplexity, and if so what?
sub_questions.answer: Yes. The paper reports VD-RHN+RE (Zilly et al. 2016), trained with reused embeddings following the paper's work, achieving validation perplexity 68.1 and test perplexity 66.0 on Penn Treebank, described as best overall.

sub_questions.q: Which Penn Treebank baselines involving cache, pointer, or ensemble does the paper list, and what test perplexities are reported for those baselines?
sub_questions.answer: The paper lists RNN+LDA+KN-5+Cache with test perplexity 92.0, Pointer Sentinel-LSTM(medium) with 70.9, 38 Large LSTMs with 68.7, and 10 Large VD-LSTMs with 68.7.
